narrative: 经典的分镜方式把主观镜头（POV）搭建成一个句子：一个人在看，我们剪到所看之物，再常常剪回反应镜头。《后窗》（Rear Window）就活在这种语法里。
摄影机就位于角色的眼睛所在之处，朝向他们所看的方向，绝不拍到他们的后脑勺。观众被迫产生代入感，因为此刻他们短暂地成为了角色本身。
它不是过肩镜头（Over-the-Shoulder Coverage）——后者保留观看者的肩膀，表达的是"与他同在"而非"成为他"。它也不是第一人称视角（First-Person）——后者让一个身体长时间占据镜头：手、呼吸、行走。
主观镜头可以只是一个静态的插入镜头。第一人称视角则是一具持续在看的身体。
主观声音（耳鸣、寂静的海滩）可以搭配主观镜头出现，也可以叠加在客观画面上。不要把听觉滤镜和这种视觉设置混为一谈。
how: 把摄影机放在指定角色的眼睛高度，朝向他们的视线方向。镜头选择要匹配他们的注意力状态：双筒望远镜式的注视用长焦，惊慌的环顾用广角。
画面中不出现角色本人的身体，除非剧情中的面罩或头盔本身就是这个光学装置（如《月光光心慌慌》/Halloween）。一旦画面里出现了肩膀，你就从主观镜头变成了过肩镜头。
提示词：what [Subject] sees, world at their eye height, no back of a head, no shoulder of the looker.
when: 用它来强制建立代入感：在这一瞥的时长里，观众就是角色本人。具体场景：先是画外的一瞥，接着是空荡的铁轨、蒸汽和灯光，都处于角色的眼睛高度。
如果同一镜头里还需要看到观看者的脸，就不要用它；应该先拍这一瞥，再接主观镜头，或者改用过肩镜头。
vs: 过肩镜头（Over-the-Shoulder Coverage）呈现近处的肩膀和远处的脸；我们是站在观看者身边。第一人称视角（First-Person）则加入手、呼吸，以及一具长期占据镜头的身体。
物体视角（Object POV）是工具或载具在看，而不是人。打破第四面墙（Fourth Wall）则是相反的注视：眼睛直视我们的镜头。
斯诺里康（SnorriCam）把摄影机绑在身体上，拍的是他们自己的脸。
examples_film: 《后窗》（Rear Window）从杰夫的脸剪到与望远镜对齐的庭院画面。《月光光心慌慌》（Halloween）开场采用了透过面罩的观察者光学视角。
《地心引力》（Gravity）切入头盔视角的观看。《拯救大兵瑞恩》（Saving Private Ryan）把视觉冲击与米勒失聪般的听觉配对；声音是它的近亲效果，而非这个镜头类型的定义本身。
mistakes: 最容易混淆的错误对象是过肩镜头（Over-the-Shoulder Coverage），或是一张望向镜头的脸。辨别标志：画面中有模糊的肩膀、后脑勺，或观看者正盯着我们。
修正方法：画面中不出现观看者本人，视线投向场景内部，高度与你刚展示的看的角色一致。如果手和枪进入画面并停留，你就滑向了第一人称视角（First-Person）。

faq.q: 电影中的主观镜头（POV）是什么？
faq.a: 主观镜头呈现的是角色从自己眼睛高度所看到的画面。摄影机代替了他们的眼睛；观看者的头部和肩膀都不会出现在画面里。

faq.q: 主观镜头 vs 过肩镜头
faq.a: 主观镜头是"成为角色"：没有角色本人的身体，只有他们所看到的世界。过肩镜头则在前景保留一侧肩膀，远处的脸清晰可见；我们是陪伴在他们身边，而不是进入他们的视线之中。

faq.q: 什么时候该用主观镜头？
faq.a: 在一瞥之后使用，当这场戏的重点是让观众代入角色所见之物时：一个庭院、一个威胁、一个面罩。不要把它当作对话戏份唯一的拍摄方式。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写主观镜头的提示词？
faq.a: 写法：What [Subject] sees at their eye height, no back of head, no looker shoulder, [object of the look] filling the frame. 并注明是谁的视角。

narrative: Classical coverage builds a POV as a sentence: a person looks, we cut to the seen, we often cut back to a reaction. Rear Window lives on that grammar.
The camera sits at their eyes, aims where they aim, and refuses the back of their head. Identification is forced because the audience is briefly the character.
It is not Over-the-Shoulder Coverage, which keeps the looker's shoulder as a claim of with, not as. It is not First-Person, which lets a body own the lens for a long ride: hands, breath, locomotion.
A POV can be a single still insert. First-person is a body that keeps seeing.
Subjective sound (a ringing ear, a mute beach) can ride with a POV or sit on an objective picture. Do not confuse a hearing filter with this optical setup.
how: Put the camera at the named character's eye height and point it along their eyeline. Match lens choice to their attention: a longer glass for binocular looking, a wider field for a panicked scan.
No owner body in frame unless a diegetic visor or mask is the optical device (Halloween). If you include a shoulder, you have left POV for OTS.
Prompt: what [Subject] sees, world at their eye height, no back of a head, no shoulder of the looker.
when: Use it to force identification: the audience is the character for the length of the look. Concrete beat: a look offscreen, then empty tracks, steam, and lamps at their eye height.
Do not use it when you still need the looker's face in the same shot; shoot the look, then the POV, or use OTS.
vs: Over-the-Shoulder Coverage shows the near shoulder and the far face; we stand with the looker. First-Person adds hands, breath, and a body that owns the lens over time.
Object POV is a tool or vehicle seeing, not a person. Fourth Wall is the opposite look: eyes into our lens.
SnorriCam straps the camera to the body and looks at their face.
examples_film: Rear Window cuts from Jeff to binocular-aligned views of the courtyard. Halloween 's opening adopts the observer's optical viewpoint through the mask.
Gravity moves into helmet-level seeing. Saving Private Ryan pairs optical shock with Miller's muted hearing; the sound is a cousin, not the definition of the shot.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Over-the-Shoulder Coverage or a face looking toward camera. Tell: a blurry shoulder, the back of a head, or the looker staring at us.
Fix: empty of the owner, eyeline into the scene, height matched to the character you just showed looking. If hands and a gun enter and stay, you drifted into First-Person.

faq.q: What is a POV shot in film?
faq.a: A POV shot shows what a character sees from their eye height. The camera stands in for their eyes; the looker's head and shoulder are not in frame.
POV is as the character: no owner body, only the seen world. Over-the-shoulder keeps a near shoulder in the foreground and the far face sharp; we are with them, not inside the look.

faq.q: When should I use a POV shot?
faq.a: Use it after a look, when identification with what they see is the beat: a courtyard, a threat, a visor. Do not use it as the only coverage of a conversation.

faq.q: How do I prompt a POV shot for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: What [Subject] sees at their eye height, no back of head, no looker shoulder, [object of the look] filling the frame. Name whose viewpoint.
